items.content_html:
Most of the commands executed during the "testing patched programs" phase of the extra-utils build don't produce any output whatsoever. Therefore, if something goes wrong in that phase, the build log is uninformative. Mitigate this by adding a set -x immediately after the "testing patched programs" message is printed, causing the shell to print an execution trace. This way we'll at least know which command failed.

I wrote this PR to help me troubleshoot issue #441269. It does not fix that issue, but I believe it is a desirable change in its own right, regardless of the eventual outcome of that issue. If this PR is accepted I would request that it also be merged to at least the 25.05 release branches.

items.content_html:
Resolves #445117, supersedes #401080 & #449578.

K3s and RKE2 share a lot of functionality, but since the nixpkgs RKE2 maintainer team is much smaller than K3s', its module tends to fall far behind - and for feature parity, code duplication across the two modules would be needed (see #401080). Merging them should make it possible for the RKE2 module to keep up with K3s without having maintainers manually copy code over.

I haven't removed or added any options, this PR is more or less just a (big) refactor. I also haven't tested the K3s module manually, but all tests in nixos/tests/{k3s,rke2} passed and I'm currently using the RKE2 module to host my site with no issues.

I've also added myself as a maintainer to RKE2.

Maintainer cc:
@rorosen @zimbatm @stefan-bordei
@NixOS/k3s

items.content_html:
Description of changes

Building a NixOS disk image results in an error when compiled without Nix tooling, as indicated by the use of the option nix.enable = false;. Disabling Nix tools through this option not only deactivates general Nix tools but also deletes NixOS installer tools. Consequently, an error is encountered in the nixos/lib/make-disk-image.nix file due to the absence of the nixos-install component.

To address this issue, it is worth noting the availability of the system.disableInstallerTools option, which serves the purpose of disabling installer tools specifically. Therefore, adjusting the configuration by using nix.enable = false; should not interfere with the presence of NixOS installation tools, as this can be managed separately through system.disableInstallerTools.

Component:

nixos/installer/tools: remove nix tooling dependency from nixos config

items.content_html:
Description of changes

With 23.11, nixos-containers won't build unless the option nixpkgs.hostPlatform is set.

Here's a minimal reproducible example:

{
  description = "nixos-containers bug demo";

  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/23.11";

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs }: {
    nixosModules.default = { pkgs, modulesPath, ... }: {
      containers.foo.config = {
        environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.hello ];
        system.stateVersion = "22.05";
      };
      system.stateVersion = "22.05";
    };

    nixosConfigurations = {
      broken = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem rec {
        pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
        modules = [
          "${nixpkgs}/nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix"
          self.nixosModules.default
        ];
      };
    };
  };
}

This results in the following error:

❯ nix flake check
error: Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set.
       You can set nixpkgs.hostPlatform in hardware-configuration.nix by re-running
       a recent version of nixos-generate-config.
       The option nixpkgs.system is still fully supported for NixOS 22.05 interoperability,
       but will be deprecated in the future, so we recommend to set nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

This PR fixes the problem by using pkgs.stdenv instead of nixpkgs.system.

    • sandbox = relaxed

    • or, for functions and "core" functionality, tests in lib/tests or pkgs/test

  • Tested compilation of all packages that depend on this change using nix-shell -p nixpkgs-review --run "nixpkgs-review rev HEAD". Note: all changes have to be committed, also see nixpkgs-review usage
  • Tested basic functionality of all binary files (usually in ./result/bin/)
  • 24.05 Release Notes (or backporting 23.05 and 23.11 Release notes)
